files.lesson.md: --- order: 16 unit: congruence node: AC9M8SP01 n1 uses: [AC9M7SP02 n1] title: Congruent triangles summary: "Congruent triangles are the same shape and size. You don't need all six parts to check: some sets of three parts fix the triangle (the congruence tests: SSS, SAS, ASA or AAS, RHS), and one set of three can fit two different triangles." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A builder cuts a hundred identical roof trusses. To check two are the same, does she need to measure every side and every angle, or are three measurements enough?" connection: truss-triangles app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8322 url: http://127.0.0.1:8322/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: tri.yml#explain-pic, caption: "AB = 8, BC = 6 and angle A = 40°: two different triangles fit, so SSA is not a congruence test." } explainClip: query: { code: "@tri.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "When SSA fails" say: "Two sides and an angle that is not between them." clip: - caption: { text: "AB = 8, angle A = 40°, BC = 9: one triangle.", say: "With BC nine, there is one triangle." } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "Make BC shorter: it can swing to two places. Two triangles.", say: "Make BC shorter. It can meet the line in two places." } - click: Make side q smaller - click: Make side q smaller - click: Make side q smaller - click: Make side q smaller - click: Make side q smaller - click: Make side q smaller - expect: { selector: "#gnote", contains: "Two different triangles" } - wait: 1600 --- Two shapes are **congruent** when one fits exactly on the other: the same shape and the same size. For triangles, matching sides and matching angles are equal. Write $\triangle ABC \equiv \triangle PQR$, with the corners in matching order. Do you need all six measurements to be sure? ## Predict: two sides and an angle ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to whether two sides and any angle fix a triangle shows whether they know the angle's position matters." check: type: predict q: "Two triangles both have sides of 8 cm and 6 cm and a 40° angle. Must they be congruent?" options: ["Not always: it depends where the angle is", "Yes: two sides and an angle are enough", "No: you always need all three sides"] actual: "Not always. With the angle between the two sides (SAS) the triangle is fixed. With the angle somewhere else (SSA), two different triangles can fit." ``` You do not need all six. These **congruence tests** each fix a triangle, so two triangles that share them are congruent. The angle between two sides is the **included angle**. | Test | Equal parts | |---|---| | **SSS** | all three sides | | **SAS** | two sides and the included angle (the angle **between** them) | | **ASA** / **AAS** | two angles and a matching side | | **RHS** | a right angle, the hypotenuse and one other side | ## Run: build from parts ```step stage: run insight: "Trying each set of parts on the board shows which sets fix one triangle and which (SSA) can give two." try: { playground: board, starter: "tri.yml#run", height: 640 } check: { type: board, text: "Try SSS, SAS and ASA, then SSA. Find parts that make two different triangles. Was your prediction right?", when: "n = 2", explain: "SSA with a short side opposite the angle: the side can meet the line in two places." } ``` Press a test to choose which parts are given, then change them with the sliders. ## Investigate: which test ```step stage: investigate insight: "Name the test from the parts and where the angle is; SSA is not a test (Tom treats it as SAS); equal angles alone give the same shape but not the same size." tasks: - check: type: question q: "In both triangles, AB = 5 cm, AC = 7 cm and angle A = 40°. Which test shows they are congruent?" options: ["SAS: angle A is between AB and AC", "SSS", "ASA", "They might not be congruent"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Only two sides are known.", "Only one angle is known.", "Angle A is between the two sides, so SAS fixes it."] explain: "Angle A is where AB and AC meet: two sides and the included angle." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#tom" text: "Tom decides two triangles are congruent. Click the line where his reasoning goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: ssa-is-test explain: "Line 3: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. Here it is not (SSA), and SSA can give two different triangles." - check: type: question q: "Two triangles both have angles of 50°, 60° and 70°. Are they congruent?" options: ["Not necessarily: they are the same shape but can be different sizes", "Yes: all three angles match", "Yes, by ASA", "No, never"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Matching angles fix the shape, not the size.", "ASA needs a side too.", "They could be congruent if a side matches as well."] explain: "Equal angles make them similar (same shape). A matching side is needed for congruence." ``` ### Which test Here is the routine. ```worked \text{AB} = 6,\ \text{BC} = 4,\ \angle B = 70^\circ :: List the equal parts. \angle B \text{ is between AB and BC} :: Where is the angle? \text{SAS} :: Two sides and the included angle. \triangle ABC \equiv \triangle PQR :: Write the congruence with matching corners in order. ``` ### Find the mistake Read Tom's working. Where is the 40° angle? ### Angles only ## Modify: tests that fail ```step stage: modify insight: "Finding parts that make no triangle, checking RHS, and reading congruence statements in order." try: { playground: board, starter: "tri.yml#asa", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "tri.yml#asa" hint: "What must the two angles add to for the two lines to meet?" check: { type: board, text: "Change the two angles so that no triangle can be made.", when: "n = 0", explain: "If angle A + angle B is 180° or more, the two lines never meet." } - starter: "tri.yml#rhs" hint: "The hypotenuse is the longest side." check: { type: board, text: "With a right angle at A, set AB = 8 and the hypotenuse BC = 10. How many triangles fit?", when: "p = 8 and r = 10", explain: "Exactly one (AC = 6): a right angle, the hypotenuse and a side fix the triangle, so RHS is a test." } - starter: "tri.yml#sss" check: { type: board, text: "Find three sides that do not make a triangle.", when: "n = 0", explain: "The two shorter sides must add to more than the longest, 2, 3 and 6 fails." } - check: type: question q: "△ABC ≡ △PQR. Which side matches BC?" options: ["QR", "PQ", "PR", "You cannot tell"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "PQ matches AB.", "PR matches AC.", "The order of the letters tells you."] explain: "B matches Q and C matches R, so BC matches QR." ``` ### No triangle ### RHS ### Sides that fail ### Matching order ## Practise: congruence tests ```step stage: practise insight: "Naming tests from given parts, mixed; treating SSA as a test is the planted slip; the angle sum review keeps triangles fresh." tasks: - check: type: question q: "Both triangles have sides 4, 6 and 7 cm. Which test?" options: ["SSS", "SAS", "RHS", "Not enough to tell"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "No angle is given.", "No right angle is given.", "Three sides are enough."] explain: "Three equal sides: SSS." - check: type: question q: "Both triangles have angles 30° and 80°, and the side opposite the 80° angle is 9 cm. Which test?" options: ["AAS", "SSS", "SAS", "Not enough to tell"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Only one side is given.", "Only one side is given.", "Two angles and a matching side are enough."] explain: "Two angles and a side that is not between them: AAS." - check: type: question q: "Both triangles have sides 9 cm and 6 cm, and a 35° angle opposite the 6 cm side (not between the two sides). Must they be congruent?" options: ["No: SSA is not a congruence test", "Yes, by SAS", "Yes, by SSS", "Yes, by RHS"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The angle is not between the sides.", "Only two sides are given.", "No right angle is given."] explain: "Two sides and a non-included angle can make two different triangles." - check: type: number q: "Review: a triangle has angles of 47° and 68°. What is the third angle, in degrees?" answer: 65 tolerance: 0 explain: "180 − 47 − 68 = 65°." ``` ### SSS ### AAS ### SSA ### Review: angle sum ## Make: exactly one ```step stage: make insight: "Finding SSA parts that give exactly one triangle shows when the ambiguous case disappears." try: { playground: board, starter: "tri.yml#ssa", height: 600 } hint: ["Too short a BC gives none; a little longer gives two.", "Try BC as long as AB, or longer."] check: { type: board, text: "With AB = 6 and angle A = 40°, find a length of BC that gives exactly one triangle.", when: "n = 1", explain: "When BC is at least as long as AB (6 cm or more), only one triangle fits." } ``` Then explain why SSA still is not a congruence test. ## Make: are two trusses the same, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A roof truss factory must know when two measurements fix a triangle; the ambiguous SSA case is where a check on paper is needed." hint: ["Is the 40° angle between the 6 m and 4 m sides, or somewhere else?", "Name the test: SSS, SAS, ASA or SSA?"] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A factory checks two roof trusses by measuring a 6 m side, a 4 m side and a 40° angle on each. The angle is opposite the 4 m side, not between the two sides. Is that enough to be sure the trusses are identical? On paper, say why, and what else to measure." steps: - ["The 40° angle is not between the 6 m and 4 m sides, so this is SSA, not SAS", "the included angle is the one between the two sides"] - ["SSA can fit two different triangles, so these trusses might not match", "with 4 m shorter than 6 m the third side can swing one of two ways"] - ["Measure the third side too (SSS), or the angle between the 6 m and 4 m sides (SAS)", "those tests fix the triangle completely"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Why is it not enough?" options: - "Two different triangles can have these same measurements" - "A truss needs all six measurements" - "40° is too small an angle to use" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Three of the right measurements are enough, such as SSS or SAS.", "The size of the angle is not the problem. Where it sits is."] criteria: - "I named the test the measurements give, SSA, and said where the angle is." - "I said two triangles can fit, so the trusses might differ." - "I named a measurement that would be enough." explain: "The angle is not between the two sides, so it is SSA, and two different trusses can fit it. Measuring all three sides (SSS) or the included angle (SAS) is enough." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The measurements are made up for the task. Real trusses have tolerances, but the idea is the same. Name the test, say whether it is enough, then choose the reason. **Also used in** - **Prefab building.** Wall frames, trusses and stair parts are cut to one drawing so any two fit the same way. - **Cut three sticks.** Three lengths make only one triangle, which is why a triangle is rigid. ```teacher summary: Students build triangles from given parts and see that SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and RHS fix one triangle while SSA can give two (AC9M8SP01, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can name the four congruence tests (SSS, SAS, ASA or AAS, RHS). - I can choose the test that shows two triangles are congruent. - I can explain why SSA is not a congruence test. struggle: Where the angle is. Ask students to point to the angle and say which sides meet there before they name a test. before: > Do the Run board yourself first: try SSA with a short BC. Students need triangle classification and the angle sum (Year 7). The one idea: a test is a set of parts that fixes the triangle, so any two triangles with those parts are congruent. The common mistake is treating SSA as SAS (Tom's mistake). The board draws every triangle the parts allow: none, one, or two (only for SSA). Wider: show two triangles formed by a rectangle's diagonal are congruent (it leads to the quadrilateral proofs in two lessons). running: - "Predict: ask where the 40° angle could be." - "Run: ask what changed between one triangle and two." - "Investigate: ask Tom which sides meet at the 40° angle." - "Modify: ask why the angles must add to less than 180°." - "Make: ask when SSA gives one triangle, and why that is not enough." - "Make on paper: ask where the 40 degrees sits, and which test that makes." stuck: - see: A student calls SSA 'SAS'. ask: Is the angle between the two sides? fix: SAS needs the included angle. - see: A student says AAA proves congruence. ask: Could a bigger triangle have the same angles? fix: Equal angles mean similar; congruence needs a side too. - see: A student matches the wrong sides. ask: Which corners match? Read the letters in order. fix: "△ABC ≡ △PQR: A with P, B with Q, C with R." stretch: Find the range of BC (with AB = 6 and angle A = 40°) that gives no triangle, two triangles and one triangle. What is special at the boundaries? support: A card with the four tests drawn, the equal parts marked. leads: > This starts AC9M8SP01. Where it leads: similar shapes (next lesson), proving quadrilateral properties, and congruence algorithms. exit: q: Two triangles have AB = PQ = 7 cm, BC = QR = 5 cm and angle B = angle Q = 60°. Are they congruent? Which test? a: "Yes, by SAS: angle B is between AB and BC." explain: > **Congruent** triangles are the same shape and size. Each **test** fixes a triangle: **SSS**, **SAS** (the angle between the sides), **ASA** or **AAS**, and **RHS**. **SSA** (an angle not between the two sides) is not a test: it can give two different triangles. Equal angles alone give the same shape, not always the same size. ```
